data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The fetch budget should be denominated in both requests and bytes, but exhaustion is recorded as a typed terminal state that includes a hash of the agent's state before the fetch that would have exceeded the budget, enabling exact replay of the exhaustion point.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Computing a state hash on every fetch may be expensive.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the agent's state is large, the hash could be a bottleneck.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the state includes non-deterministic elements (e.g., random seeds), the hash must be computed over deterministic components only.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When a fetch would exceed either limit, the agent records the budget counters, the limits, and a state hash (e.g., of the agent's memory, excluding the budget counters themselves). This state hash allows an auditor to replay the run up to the exact point of exhaustion and verify that the same fetch would be attempted. This ensures the terminal is auditable and replayable even if the budget counters are not part of the state hash.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
